metadata.title: Research by application
metadata.description: Application-specific research pages connecting the MSEI research themes to microrobotics, dexterous manipulation, medical robotics and scientific instrumentation.

applications.title: Optical and magnetic microrobotics
applications.summary: Optical and magnetic actuation, microscopy and adaptive control for precise manipulation at small scales.
applications.lead: We study how miniature robots can perceive, move and manipulate when forces are applied from outside the robot and sensing is provided through a microscope.
applications.introduction: Optical tweezers and magnetic fields provide complementary ways to actuate small robots. Our work brings fabrication, force generation, image-based perception and interactive control together, with an emphasis on how physical design changes the manipulation that a platform can achieve.
applications.question: How can external fields and visual feedback enable dexterous manipulation at small scales?
applications.connection: This application makes the relationship between embodiment and intelligence explicit. The robot’s geometry and actuation determine its available motions; microscopy estimates its state; learning and control turn those physical capabilities into manipulation.

applications.caption: AI-generated concept illustration of optical and magnetic microrobotics; structures are not to scale.

focusAreas.title: Optical manipulation and perception
focusAreas.description: We combine fabricated microrobots with optical tweezers, investigate how laser forces generate controlled motion, and use learned microscopy models to estimate pose and depth.

focusAreas.title: Magnetic navigation and shared control
focusAreas.description: We investigate field-driven navigation and operator assistance in constrained environments. Learning-based control and immersive interfaces support steering, while bimanual shared control adapts the assistance provided by multiple magnetic sources.

focusAreas.title: Physical design and reconfiguration
focusAreas.description: We study how geometry, materials and magnetic functionalisation affect controllable motion. Related modular magnetic work examines assembly, locomotion and shape changes at the millimetre scale.

applications.evidenceNote: Experiments span different physical scales and platforms. The modular reconfiguration study concerns millirobots; the optical work concerns microrobots. Navigation in a vascular phantom or simulated environment is research validation, not evidence of clinical use.
applications.nextDirection: A longer-term question is when changing a robot’s physical configuration adds capability beyond adapting its controller. Answering it requires measured forces, reliable state estimation and comparisons under the same task conditions.

applications.title: Dexterous robotic manipulation
applications.summary: Tactile sensors, integrated grippers and adaptable learning for contact-rich robot tasks.
applications.lead: We connect tactile hardware and robot learning so that manipulation can respond to the object, the contact and the task.
applications.introduction: Contact-rich tasks require robots to use information that images alone may not reveal. Our research combines visual and tactile perception with sensor and gripper design, then studies how demonstrations, simulation and multimodal policies can produce adaptable manipulation skills.
applications.question: How can a robot use touch and vision to adapt its manipulation to changing objects and conditions?
applications.connection: This application connects physical sensing with learned action. Sensor materials and geometry shape the observations available to a policy; learning methods determine how those observations are used when an object, task or sensing setup changes.
applications.alt: Conceptual tactile robotic gripper interacting with a deformable object beside an abstract sensory representation.
applications.caption: AI-generated concept illustration of tactile manipulation; the inset is not experimental data.

focusAreas.title: Tactile perception and sensor design
focusAreas.description: We develop sensors and materials that capture complementary information about interaction. Multimodal interpretation, in-sensor processing and inverse design connect the physical sensing surface to usable perceptual information.

focusAreas.title: Integrated contact-rich manipulation
focusAreas.description: We study how tactile sensing can be incorporated into grippers and coordinated robot actions. The aim is to connect what is sensed during contact with the actions needed to maintain and change that interaction.

focusAreas.title: Adaptation with limited new data
focusAreas.description: We investigate how learned skills and tactile representations change across objects, scenes and sensors. Demonstration-efficient adaptation and cross-sensor benchmarks make the transfer problem measurable.

applications.nextDirection: We aim to make adaptation more data-efficient and easier to evaluate across sensing hardware and robot embodiments, while retaining the physical information needed for precise interaction.

applications.title: Medical robotics and microsurgery
applications.summary: Shared control, adaptive motion scaling and immersive interfaces for surgical robotics research.
applications.lead: We develop robotic assistance that responds to the task and the operator during delicate, precise manipulation.
applications.introduction: Surgical and microsurgical research provides a demanding setting for studying how human judgement and robot precision can work together. Our work examines control allocation, motion scaling, haptic feedback and digital-twin interfaces on research platforms and in training tasks.
applications.question: How should robotic assistance adapt as a precise manipulation task and the operator’s needs change?
applications.connection: Here, adaptive physical intelligence includes the human operator. Perception estimates task context, learning transfers useful motion patterns, and control adjusts assistance while the operator remains part of the interaction.
applications.alt: Concept illustration of robotic instruments positioned around a synthetic surgical phantom in a research laboratory.
applications.caption: AI-generated concept illustration of a medical-robotics research platform using a synthetic phantom; not a clinical photograph or experimental result.

focusAreas.title: Context-aware shared control
focusAreas.description: We investigate how a robot can adjust its contribution during different task contexts. Demonstrations collected in simulation support learned motions, while context recognition informs the allocation of control.

focusAreas.title: Adaptive microsurgical motion
focusAreas.description: We study the mapping between an operator’s input and the robot’s tool motion. Adaptive motion scaling and damping address the changing precision demands of delicate tasks.

focusAreas.title: Immersive interfaces and research platforms
focusAreas.description: Digital twins, mixed reality and haptic feedback provide different ways for an operator to perceive remote interaction. Microsurgical platforms and skill-assessment methods support repeatable research and training.

applications.evidenceNote: The work described here concerns research systems, user studies and training or experimental tasks. It does not establish clinical deployment or a replacement for clinical judgement. Mixed-reality teleoperation is a related enabling method, rather than a claim of a clinically validated system.
applications.nextDirection: We aim to investigate assistance that responds more explicitly to uncertainty, changing contact and operator workload, with evaluation that considers both manipulation performance and the human experience.

evidenceQuestions: What task does the operator perform, and what assistance does the robot provide?
How are accuracy, interaction and operator performance evaluated in the study?
Which results are specific to the research platform or user-study setting?

applications.title: Robotics for scientific experiments
applications.summary: Image-guided micromanipulation, pipette localisation and open perception benchmarks for scientific workflows.
applications.lead: We develop robotic perception and manipulation tools that address practical bottlenecks in microscopy-based experiments.
applications.introduction: Scientific instruments must connect an observation to a precisely controlled physical action. Our work studies localisation of multiple pipettes, pose and depth perception under a microscope, and reproducible datasets that allow these perception methods to be compared.
applications.question: How can robotic perception make delicate experimental operations more repeatable and easier to automate?
applications.connection: This application connects the lab’s sensing and learning methods to experimental practice. Reliable state estimates are a prerequisite for useful control, and the mechanics of a tool or microscopic object determine which observations and actions are possible.
applications.alt: Concept illustration of a microscope, micromanipulators and sample chamber in a precision experimentation laboratory.
applications.caption: AI-generated concept illustration of microscopy and robotic instrumentation; not a photograph of a completed autonomous laboratory or experimental result.

focusAreas.title: Multi-pipette localisation
focusAreas.description: For robot-assisted patch-clamp research, we study how image processing and learning can locate several pipette tips. The approach combines visibility enhancement with coarse detection and fine coordinate estimation.

focusAreas.title: Microscopy-based pose and depth
focusAreas.description: We investigate perception of small, low-contrast structures under an optical microscope. Physics-informed simulation and learning help address the cost of obtaining and labelling experimental images.

focusAreas.title: Reproducible experimental foundations
focusAreas.description: Open datasets, benchmarks and code make perception studies easier to compare and build upon. Our work on biological micromanipulation also examines how sensing, physical tools and control need to be considered together.

applications.evidenceNote: Multi-pipette localisation is a perception contribution within a larger experimental workflow. The datasets and simulations support method development and evaluation; they are not evidence of a complete autonomous scientific laboratory.
applications.nextDirection: Our longer-term direction is to connect reliable perception and adaptive manipulation with the selection of informative experiments. This remains a research agenda built on the instrumentation and perception studies above.
